question.text: If the Put-Call Ratio (PCR) is greater than 1, it indicates that:

answer.text: The number of outstanding put options exceeds the number of outstanding call options
The market is strongly bullish with more call buyers
Options are more expensive than futures contracts
The number of call options traded exceeds put options

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series XII page 212, PCR is defined as the number of outstanding put options divided by the number of outstanding call options. If PCR is greater than one, outstanding puts exceed outstanding calls. The Trap: PCR strictly compares outstanding put options to outstanding call options, not traded volumes and not options versus futures pricing. PCR greater than one does not by itself indicate a bullish market with more call buyers. Note: Anchor the answer on the page 212 ratio definition (outstanding puts / outstanding calls) rather than on any directional trading interpretation.
